title: Verb 'to be' (am/is/are) / Verb 'to be' (am/is/are)
bridge: En wolof, ci suñu làkk, 'to be' du jëkkër ci 'ser' ak 'estar' te 'am/is/are'. Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' yi ngi ci 'am' (naa), 'is' (naa) ak 'are' (naa) ci 'I', 'he/she/it' ak 'you/we/they'. Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' du taxawul bu baax ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk. Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' du taxawul bu baax ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk.
rule: Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' ci 'am/is/are' ci 'présent' ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk. Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' ci 'am/is/are' ci 'présent' ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk. Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' ci 'am/is/are' ci 'présent' ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk.

concept_examples.translation: Danga bëgg? (literal: Danga bëgg ci bëgg?)

common_error.explanation: Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' du taxawul bu baax ci suñu làkk ci suñu làkk. 'Am/is/are' du taxawul bu baax ci suñu làkk.

examples.note: Ci suñu làkk, 'to be' yi ngi taxawul ci 'subject' ak 'verb' ci 'questions'.

title: Pronoms personels (Ma, ya, moom, ñu, ñu, nu, ñu)
bridge: In Wolof, personal pronouns are similar: ma, ya, moom, ñu, ñu, nu, ñu. The main difference is that in English, you always use the pronoun as the subject, even when in Wolof it might be omitted: 'Maa ngi fi' (not just 'ngi fi'). Also, be careful not to confuse 'he' and 'she' — in English they refer to biological gender, not grammatical gender as in Spanish.
rule: The personal pronouns in English are: I (ma), you (ya/ñu), he (moom), she (ñu), it (lu), we (nu), they (ñu). 'Lu' is used for objects, animals, and concepts. 'Ya' can be singular or plural. The subject is never omitted in English.

concept_examples.translation: Lu nekk ci woon (lu nekk ci woon).

common_error.correct: He is a teacher. / She is a teacher.
common_error.explanation: In Wolof, we say 'Lu doom' omitting the subject, but in English the pronoun is mandatory. You must always say 'He is...' or 'She is...'.

examples.note: 'Lu' génn ci yaram, ci mbir ci woon.

translations.wo: Pronoms personels (Ma, ya, moom, ñu, ñu, nu, ñu)

title: Articles (a/an, the) / Atikulo (a/an, the)
bridge: Xoolal ci suñu, ci waloñu du gotul: 'un/una' (ndaxmi) ak 'el/la/los/las' (ndaxmi). Li ngi ci waloñu, ci suñu, mooy nu ko wax ci 'the' ci maam ci joxe ndaxmi jëkkëru (ñunga wax 'Life is beautiful', mënul 'The life is beautiful'). Bëgg naa ko wax ci jëkkëru ak liggéey yi, nu ko wax 'a' walla 'an' ci suñu: 'I am a teacher' (ci suñu, nu wax 'Soy profesor' tekk ci atikulo).
rule: Nu ko wax 'a' ci ñuutal ci jëkkëru yi (a book, a car). Nu ko wax 'an' ci ñuutal ci woy woy (an apple, an hour — 'h' mi nu ko waxul). Nu ko wax 'the' ci maam ci li diñu wax ko waxe ci li di naan ko waxe ci li di naan ci li di naan ci li di naan. Mënul ko wax 'the' ci maam ci jëkkëru jëkkëru (Love is important, mënul 'The love').

common_error.explanation: Ci suñu, nu wax 'Soy profesor' tekk ci atikulo. Ci suñu, ak liggéey yi, nu ko wax 'a' walla 'an'.

examples.note: Nu ko wax 'a' ci ñuutal ci jëkkëru yi.
Nu ko wax 'an' ci ñuutal ci woy woy.
'The' mooy ko wax ci li di naan ko waxe ci li di naan ci li di naan.
Ci jëkkëru jëkkëru, mënul ko wax 'the'.

title: Plurales regulares e irregulares básicos / Plurales gu bërë gu mag gi
bridge: Ci español, ñu xëpp formes plurales ngir xàq -s ɓa -es (casa → casas, reloj → relojes). Ci angiils, moo taxaw ci sama yàq: màgg gi ñu xëpp xàq -s (book → books), ɓa ñu ngi dégg ngone si yékkoonu woon ngir: si xàccu gi ngi ànd ak -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z, ñu xàq -es (bus → buses, watch → watches). Ɗalee ca plurales irregulares (child → children, foot → feet) ñu ngi am solo ci yékkoonu woon ɓa ñu ngi joxe ci solo.
rule: Règles ci plurales gu bërë gu mag: 1) Xàq -s (cat → cats). 2) Xàq -es si xàccu gi ngi ànd ak -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z (box → boxes, dish → dishes). 3) Si ànd ak -y ɓa ci moomu ànd ak consonne, àndu -y ɓa -ies (city → cities). 4) Si ànd ak -f ɓa -fe, ñu ngi dégg ngone si yékkoonu woon ci -ves (wolf → wolves, knife → knives). Plurales irregulares mooy si yékkoonu woon: child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, man → men, woman → women, mouse → mice, sheep → sheep (sama), fish → fish (sama ci sama xaral).

common_error.explanation: Ci español, plurales gu bërë gu mag gi ñu ngi solo (niño → niños), ɓa ci angiils 'child' mooy si yékkoonu woon ɓa àndu gu plural gi mooy 'children'. Moo taxaw ci màgg gi ñu ngi dégg ngone si yékkoonu woon ci xàq -s.

examples.note: Plural gu bërë gu mag ngir xàq -s.
Xàccu gi ngi ànd ak -x xàq -es.
Gu plural gi sama ci gu singular.

translations.wo: Plurales gu bërë gu mag gi

title: Presente simple (I eat, you eat, he eats) / Dëgg-dëgg (Maa ngi ngi, yaa ngi ngi, ku ngi ngi)
bridge: Ak español, ñu ngi defar dëgg-dëgg péey ak yoonal: 'Maa ngi pizza tus los días'. Ak angiis, moo leegi, ndax kat bu njëkk a ngi (ku, yaa, ku) ñu ngi defar -s ak verb (ku ngi ngi, yaa dàkk). Ñu ngi defar itam ak auxiliar 'do/does' péey ak wuññi yi ak wuññi yi, bu njëkk a ngi ak español ñu ngi defar '¿...?' ak entonación, bu leegi, ak angiis, bu njëkk a ngi.
rule: Dëgg-dëgg defar na ak verb bu njëkk péey ak yoonal, ndax bu njëkk a ngi (ku, yaa, ku), ñu ngi defar -s (bu leegi -es bu njëkk a ngi ak -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z). Péey ak wuññi yi ak wuññi yi, ñu ngi defar 'do' (ak I, yaa, ñu, ñu) bu leegi 'does' (ak ku, yaa, ku) + verb bu njëkk (bu leegi -s). Ej: 'Maa ngi ngi', 'Ku ngi ngi', 'Do yaa ngi ngi?', 'Yaa bu ngi ngi'.

common_error.explanation: Ak español, bu njëkk a ngi (ku) bu leegi defar special ak dëgg-dëgg (ku ngi), bu leegi ak angiis, ñu ngi defar -s (ku ngi ngi). Moo leegi bu njëkk a ngi ak yoonal yi.

examples.original: She reads a book every day.
examples.translation: Yaa dégg ak buk ak 8 saa.

examples.note: Ñu ngi defar 'don't' + verb bu njëkk.

title: Adverbios de frecuencia (always, sometimes, never) / Adyafi yi bëgg yi
bridge: Àddina, adyafi yi bëgg yi njëkk 'siempre', 'a veces' ak 'nunca' dafay jëfandikoo ngir jëfandikoo verbe: 'Man jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk' ba àddina ci verbe bi njëkk. Ànglës, làkk wi manees na koo xam ne: dafay jëfandikoo ngir jëfandikoo verbe bu njëkk (I always eat pizza), ba ca verbe 'to be' (I am always tired). Xalima yi wër: àddina, manees na koo wër adyafi yi bëgg yi ci biir orasi, ba ànglës, moo leen di wër.
rule: Adyafi yi bëgg yi njëkk yi: always (siempre), usually (normalmente), often (a menudo), sometimes (a veces), rarely (raramente), never (nunca). Dafay jëfandikoo ngir jëfandikoo verbe bu njëkk (I always go to school), ba ca verbe 'to be' (I am always happy). Ci ànd ak xalaat, dafay jëfandikoo ngir jëfandikoo sujets (Do you always eat breakfast?).

concept_examples.text: I always drink coffee in the morning.
concept_examples.translation: Man jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk ci suba.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɔːlweɪz drɪŋk ˈkɒfi ɪn ðə ˈmɔːnɪŋ/

concept_examples.translation: Moom, nunu wër adyaf bu njëkk.

concept_examples.text: They sometimes go to the cinema.
concept_examples.translation: Ñoom, ñu jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk ci sinema.
Ku jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk ci xay?

common_error.explanation: Àddina, manees na koo wër 'Man jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk' ba 'Man jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk'. Ànglës, adyafi yi bëgg yi dafay jëfandikoo ngir jëfandikoo verbe bu njëkk (always eat). Moo leen di wër adyaf bu njëkk àddina ci ànglës.

examples.original: I always get up at 7 am.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɔːlweɪz ɡet ʌp æt ˈsevən æm/
examples.translation: Man jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk ci 7 ci suba.
Moom, ñu jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk ci télé.
Man jëfandikoo adyaf bu njëkk ci xay bu njëkk.
Moom, nunu wër adyaf bu njëkk.
examples.note: Adyafi yi bëgg yi dafay jëfandikoo ngir jëfandikoo verbe 'to be'.

title: Have got / Has got
bridge: Àdduna, ñu ngi ci jamono ci ñaari bàkk: 'have' (I have a car) ak 'have got' (I have got a car). 'Have got' moom la guy sax ci angale, mooy wi ñu ngi ci defaroon ci jamono ju ñaaw. Ci mbooleem ak wàcc, 'have got' ngi def ko 'have' ngirum, ndax 'do/does' duñu ngi def. Naka noonu, 'I haven't got a car' ak 'Have you got a car?'
rule: Have got / Has got ngi def ci jamono ci ñaari: ci ñoom, ndimbal ak sàmm. Afirmativo: I/you/we/they have got, he/she/it has got. Negativo: I/you/we/they have not got (haven't got), he/she/it has not got (hasn't got). Wàcce: Have I/you/we/they got? Has he/she/it got? 'Do/does' duñu ngi def. Ci wàcc yu bari: Yes, I have / No, I haven't. Ñu ngi def ko ci jamono ju ñaaw, ndax ñaar yeneen jamono ñu ngi def 'have' yi

concept_examples.text: I have got a new phone.
concept_examples.translation: Maa ngi fi indi niiw telefòn
Yaa ngi fi indi niiw dégg
Nga def naa ngi fi indi niiw wàll
Nga dàkknaa ngi fi indi niiw kàsu

common_error.explanation: Àdduna, 'ñu ñaaw' ngi def ko 'have' ak 'have got'. Moom 'have got' ngi def ko 'got' wi, duñu def ko 'get'. Def 'I have get' moom kàccoor la, waaye ñu ngi def ko 'get' wi, ndax ñu ngi def ko 'have got' ci jamono

examples.original: We have got a big house.
examples.translation: Ñu ngi fi indi niiw kër ñaaw
examples.note: Ñu ngi def 'have got' ci jamono ci ñaari

examples.translation: Maa ngi fi indi niiw sàkk
examples.note: Ñu ngi def 'has got' ci jamono ci ñaari ci ñoom

examples.translation: Yaa dàkknaa ngi fi indi niiw wàll
Nga def naa ngi fi indi niiw ñoom?
examples.note: Wàcc ngi def ko 'have/has' ak ñoom

title: Preposiciones de lugar (in, on, under, next to) / Wànde yi (ci, ngone, def, ci diggante)
bridge: Ñi ko waxe woy wolof, ñi def ko 'ci' ak 'ngone' ak 'def' ak 'ci diggante'. Ñi angale, ñakk ñu xamme ngone preposisyon yi, te xool it xool, 'in' woy espas ci bëgg, 'on' woy superfisi, 'under' woy def, 'next to' woy ci diggante. Woy def it 'ci kër' mooy 'on the corner', dina 'in'.
rule: Preposisyon yi wànde: in (ci, espas bëgg), on (ngone, superfisi), under (def), next to (ci diggante). Woy ñatti: behind (ca), in front of (ci mel), between (ci wetu). Ñi angale britannik, ñi def ko 'on the bus', 'on the train', waaye 'in the car'. Ñi wàcc: 'Where is the cat?' → 'It is under the table.'

concept_examples.text: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the bed.
The supermarket is next to the bank.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈsuːpəmɑːkɪt ɪz nekst tə ðə bæŋk/

common_error.explanation: Ñi ko waxe woy wolof, ñi def ko 'ci otobis' ci wàcc yi, waaye ñi angale, ñakk ñu xamme 'on' ngone preposisyon yi, dina 'in'. 'In' woy def ko woy kër, taksi.

examples.original: The milk is in the fridge.
examples.note: Ñi def ko 'in' ci espas bëgg.

examples.original: The keys are on the table.
My shoes are under the chair.
The school is next to the church.
examples.phonetic: /ðə skuːl ɪz nekst tə ðə tʃɜːtʃ/
examples.translation: Ecole yi ngi ci diggante kër
examples.note: Ñi def ko 'next to' ci diggante.

title: Demostrativos (this, that, these, those) / Wàlliyu (bii, baa, ñi, ñee)
bridge: Àdduna, ñuul seen 'bii' (dogg), 'baa' (ndàkk), 'ñi' (guddi) ak 'ñee' (guddi guddi). Àngale, ñuul seen na 'this' (bii, singular) ak 'these' (ñi, plural) dogg; 'that' (baa, singular) ak 'those' (ñee, plural) ndàkk. Bokk nañu ngéen xamalee ngi ci wàlliyu seeni àdduna, ndax ñu ngi dégg ngéen xamalee 'baa' ak 'ñi' àngale, waaye ñu ngi dégg ngéen xamalee 'this' ngéen xamalee yépp, ndax dégg na ngéen xamalee, waaye ñu ngi dégg ngéen xamalee 'these' (ñi) ak 'this' (bii) ngéen xamalee ngi dégg ngéen xamalee.
rule: Ñu ngi dégg 'this' ngéen xamalee yépp (bii, singular). Ñu ngi dégg 'these' ngéen xamalee yépp (ñi, plural). Ñu ngi dégg 'that' ngéen xamalee ndàkk (baa, singular). Ñu ngi dégg 'those' ngéen xamalee ndàkk (ñee, plural). Waaye ñu ngi dégg ngéen xamalee ngi dégg ngéen xamalee: 'This is my friend' (yépp, ngéen xamalee) ak 'That is my house' (ndàkk, ngéen xamalee).

common_error.explanation: Àdduna, 'bii' ak 'baa' dégg na ngéen xamalee, waaye ñu ngi dégg ngéen xamalee 'this' ngéen xamalee ñi (plural) ngéen xamalee, waaye ñu ngi dégg ngéen xamalee 'these' /ðiːz/ ak 'this' /ðɪs/. Dégg na ngéen xamalee 'this' bii (singular) ak 'these' ñi (plural).

title: Can (habilidad y permiso) / Dëgg
bridge: Àddina, ñu ngi ci wàll 'poder' péet loxol habilité ('puedo nadar') ak permiso ('¿puedo ir?'). Àddina, 'can' itam moo taxawal nañu benn ci ñaari yoon. Bari naa tàmbali mooy 'can' dafa amul ci ñaari ñatti (he can, she can) ak dafa amul 'to' ci des (I can swim, buñu 'I can to swim'). Buñu, péet taxawal ak négatiif, ñu ngi ci wàll 'do/does' waaye ñu defaroon ci mbooloom (Can you swim?) ak ñu defaroon 'not' (I cannot / can't). Moo verbe modale, kon ñu ngi def ci wàll verbe infinitif ci anam 'to'.
rule: 'Can' amul na: 1) habilité (I can play the piano), 2) permiso (Can I go to the bathroom?), 3) posibilidad (It can rain tomorrow). Amul na ci ñaari ñatti. Afirmatif: I/you/he/she/it/we/they can + verbe bare. Négatif: cannot (can't) + verbe bare. Taxawal: Can + sujets + verbe bare? Réponses courtes: Yes, I can / No, I can't.

common_error.explanation: Àddina, ñu ngi wàll 'puedo cantar' ci anam preposicion. Àddina, 'can' amul na ci wàll verbe infinitif CI ANAM 'to'. Wàll 'can to' mooy kàggam gu mag ci analogie ak ñaari verbe ñoom ñi ngi def ci wàll 'to' (want to, need to).

examples.original: Can they come? Yes, they can.

title: Preguntas con 'wh-' (what, where, who, when) / Naatale ak wh- (kii, féete, këram, nataa)
bridge: Àddee ñu woolu, ñu jàngi naatale ak almaane wéeru kii, féete, këram, nataa. Àddee ñu angalteer, ñu leeral kii (kii), féete (féete), këram (këram), nataa (nataa). Mbooloom xam na: Almaane wh- + verb saa (walla verb to be) + suufu + verb wéeru? Nataa ñu ci yonne: 'Where do you live?' (Féete ngi def?). Dëkk bu njëkk ci ñu woolu ñu jàngi, mooy woolu verb saa 'do/does' ci présent simple, walla wéeru nguur gi ci naatale yàq.
rule: Naatale wh- ñu jàngi kóllëre: 1) Ak verb to be: Almaane wh- + am/is/are + suufu? (Féete ngi def bank bi?). 2) Ak 'can': Almaane wh- + can + suufu + verb? (Kii ngi amul?). 3) Ak présent simple (verb wéeru wër): Almaane wh- + do/does + suufu + verb wéeru? (Kii ngi jàng?). 4) Naatale yàq (ci 'Can you tell me...', 'Do you know...'), xoloom xam na suufu + verb (déedéet gi): 'Can you tell me where the station is?' (Féete ngi def stasiyon bi?).

common_error.wrong: Can you tell me where is the station?
common_error.correct: Can you tell me where the station is?
common_error.explanation: Àddee ñu woolu, naatale yàq, ñu jàngi xoloom xam na naatale wéeru: 'Ñu ngi ko jàngal féete ngi def stasiyon bi?'. Àddee ñu angalteer, naatale yàq, xoloom xam na suufu + verb, déedéet gi. Moom kay ngone ci ñu woolu ñu jàngi.

title: There is / There are
bridge: Ci español, ñu ngi def 'hay' ñu nekk cee wax: 'hay'. Ci angiis, ñu ngi def ndeem: 'there is' (singular) ak 'there are' (plural). Ndeem bu njëkk a xew, ndax mbooloom bu ñu ngi def. Baat ba: 'There is a book on the table' (Hay un libro sobre la mesa), 'There are two books on the table' (Hay dos libros sobre la mesa). Ñu ngi leen def ci pëkk: 'Is there a bank near here?' ak 'Are there any restaurants?'. Yërëng gu ñu am solo ci ñi ngi def 'there is/are' ak 'have' (ñu ngi def 'The house has a garden' ba 'There is a garden in the house').
rule: Ñu ngi def 'There is' ci mbooloom yu seen ak yu bari (There is some water). Ñu ngi def 'There are' ci mbooloom yu seen yu ñaari (There are three chairs). Ci pëkk: Is there...? / Are there...? Ci njëkk: There isn't / There aren't. Leegi ñu ngi def ci 'any' ci pëkk ak njëkk: 'Is there any milk?' (¿Hay leche?) ak 'There isn't any milk' (No hay leche).

concept_examples.text: There is a cat in the garden.
concept_examples.translation: Hay un gato en el jardín.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə kæt ɪn ðə ˈɡɑːdən/

concept_examples.text: There are two chairs in the kitchen.
concept_examples.translation: Hay dos sillas en la cocina.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːr tuː tʃeəz ɪn ðə ˈkɪtʃɪn/

concept_examples.text: Is there a bank near here?
There aren't any students in the class.
concept_examples.translation: No hay estudiantes en la clase.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːnt ˈeni ˈstjuːdənts ɪn ðə klɑːs/

common_error.wrong: In my house have a garden.
common_error.correct: There is a garden in my house.
common_error.explanation: Ci español, ñu ngi def 'Mi casa tiene un jardín' ñu ngi def 'tener', ba ci angiis, ñu ngi def 'there is/are', dina 'have', ci defar ndaw. Moo ngi def 'My house has a garden' (tener) waxe, ba 'there is' moom la ñu ngi def ci defar ndaw ci benn lëgg.

examples.original: There is a phone on the desk.
examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɪz ə fəʊn ɒn ðə desk/
examples.translation: Hay un teléfono en el escritorio.

examples.original: There are three cars in the street.
examples.phonetic: /ðeər ɑːr θriː kɑːrz ɪn ðə striːt/
examples.translation: Hay tres coches en la calle.

levels.label: Questions with Is there / Are there
levels.translation: Preguntas con Is there / Are there

examples.original: Are there any eggs in the fridge?
examples.phonetic: /ɑːr ðeər ˈeni eɡz ɪn ðə frɪdʒ/

examples.original: There isn't any sugar in the cupboard.
examples.phonetic: /ðeər ˈɪzənt ˈeni ˈʃʊɡər ɪn ðə ˈkʌbəd/
examples.translation: No hay azúcar en el armario.

translations.wo: Ci angiis, ñu ngi def 'there is' ak 'there are' ci defar ndaw.
